title: Homocystinuria
everyday_terms: blood clots at a young age
summary: Homocystinuria means the body cannot process a building block of protein called methionine properly. A substance called homocysteine builds up and can affect the eyes, bones, brain and blood vessels.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the CBS gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has homocystinuria. Found early, it is managed with a special diet and other care from a specialist team, which can prevent many problems.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has homocystinuria. Could I be a carrier?
What does a test for the CBS gene involve?
card_summary: A protein building block isn't processed properly. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Can affect the eyes, bones and blood vessels; managed by specialist teams.
care: Specialist metabolic and eye clinics, dietitians, genetic counselling and family support groups.
counsellor_questions: Which carrier test is right for me?
